subject: NexaLab VPC/on‑prem qualification — synthesis & next owners
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@nexalab.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: NexaLab VPC/on‑prem qualification — synthesis & next owners

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Wanted to capture a concise synthesis from our call and the concrete next steps so nothing slips. Please reply with corrections or any missing contacts.

Quick summary of what you shared (pain + goals):
- Regulatory driver: NexaLab needs data residency in US-only regions and an ability to run an air‑gapped inference posture for certain PHI workloads.
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference costs and latency when routing to hosted endpoints; procurement + security want a hosting model with clear egress controls and auditability.
- Networking constraints: outbound firewall rules, no public inbound IPs for the private cluster, preferred private link or direct connect, and strict whitelist for egress destinations.
- Timeline and priority: procurement window opens mid‑Nov; pilot target = low‑risk inference use case by end of Q4.

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC-hosted or on‑prem appliance) with a customer-managed control plane, KMS integration, and optional air‑gapped data path for PHI-heavy requests.
- Two-step engagement: 1) qualification (network/residency/security), 2) pilot (1–2 model endpoints + traffic shaping).

Open technical questions we flagged on the call (please confirm):
1) Which subnets will allow outbound traffic, and can you share an egress acceptance list (FQDNs/IP ranges)?
2) Do you have an internal bastion/jump host pattern or will we set up a management tunnel from Redwood?
3) Which KMS/HSM provider will you use for key material (AWS KMS / HashiCorp / YubiHSM)?
4) Is there an internal SOC/infosec reviewer we should include for the third‑party risk questionnaire?

Action items / owners / rough ETA:
- Alex (NexaLab): share a one‑page network sketch showing subnet boundaries, expected NAT/GW egress points, and any existing private link endpoints — due: 2029‑08‑22. (Attachment template: nexalab-network-sketch-request.docx)
- Marissa (Redwood): schedule a 60‑minute technical deep‑dive (network + security) with NexaLab infra and infosec — proposed windows below.
- Ben (Redwood): prepare a draft scope for the pilot (models, traffic profile, cost estimate) and a checklist for air‑gapped playbook.

Proposed deep‑dive slots (PST):
- Tue 8/20 10:00–11:00
- Wed 8/21 14:00–15:00
- Thu 8/22 09:00–10:00

Attachments: redwood-private-hosting-checklist.pdf (pilot checklist), nexalab-network-sketch-request.docx (template to populate).

If any of the above needs correction, call it out and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll assume we’ll target 8/20 or 8/21 for the tech dive and Alex will push the network sketch.

—
Jordan Blake

From: Alex Gardner <alex.gardner@nexalab.health>

Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexaLab VPC/on‑prem qualification — synthesis & next owners

Jordan — thanks for the writeup, this is very helpful. A few clarifications and one correction:

1) Timeline: procurement window opens 11/10, but legal wants the SOW signed earlier — aim for a commercial term draft by 10/15 if possible.
2) Network sketch: I’ll attach our sketch but it’s a little rough; we have a private link to our AWS account and a NAT layer in a central VPC that handles egress to partner services. We prefer private link over direct connect for the pilot.
3) Air‑gap nuance: only the PHI inference path needs strict air‑gapping; non‑PHI can go through a private Redwood endpoint in our VPC.
4) KMS: we use AWS KMS with a customer‑managed CMK.

I’m looping in Priya (head of infra) for the deep technical questions and she’ll be the day‑to‑day reviewer for the questionnaire. Priya — can you confirm the best times next week for a technical sync?

I’ll aim to get the network sketch to Jordan by 8/21 EOD.

Thanks —
Alex Gardner
VP IT & Infrastructure
NexaLab Health

Appreciate the clarifications — helpful to know the split between PHI vs non‑PHI traffic and that you’re on AWS KMS. Updated next steps based on Alex/Priya notes: 

- Alex/Priya: deliver network sketch focused on egress points and private link architecture — due: 2029‑08‑21 EOD.
- Marissa: will send a calendar invite for a 60‑minute tech dive; proposing Tue 8/20 10:00 PST as primary.
- Ben: will draft the pilot SOW + cost banding, and a short commercial checklist for the 10/15 milestone.
- Jordan: will send the third‑party security questionnaire and a short pre‑read on the air‑gap options we typically deliver.

Marissa — please send invites and include the following internal NexaLab roles if available: network lead, security engineer, and procurement SME.

Thanks everyone — goal is to have the qualification packet in place by 10/01 so commercial negotiations can proceed.

—
Jordan
